body: President Donald Trump visited the construction site of the new White House ballroom on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, signing the final steel beam before a crane lifted it into place on the roof. The visit was his first public appearance since the November 3 midterm elections, in which Democrats made sweeping gains.

The ballroom is being built on the site of the East Wing, which was constructed in 1902 and demolished beginning in October 2025. Trump has described the project as one of the largest and most beautiful ballrooms in the world, with 50-foot ceilings, marble floors and Corinthian columns. The White House has put the cost at about $400 million, funded by the president and private donors, though other published estimates have been higher.

The project has faced legal challenges. The National Trust for Historic Preservation sued in December 2025, arguing that the demolition and construction were unlawful without legally required reviews. In August 2026, the Supreme Court stayed a lower-court injunction, allowing construction to continue while the case proceeds.

Critics, including preservation groups, have objected to the demolition of the historic East Wing and the scale of the new structure. The White House has said the project is tied to the security of the president and the White House grounds, and that the ballroom will serve presidents for generations to come.
imageCredit: The White House, Washington, D.C. — Photo: Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of the White House. No free photo of the ballroom construction itself was available.
summary: President Donald Trump visited the construction site of the new East Wing ballroom on November 4, signing the final steel beam before it was lifted into place.
title: Trump Showcases White House Ballroom as Final Steel Beam Is Raised

body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo's remake of the 1998 Nintendo 64 classic, launched on November 5, 2026, exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2. The game is listed at $59.99 in the United States.

The remake rebuilds the original's visuals with what Nintendo describes as a puppet-show look, and adds an orchestral soundtrack, fully voiced cutscenes, expanded dialogue and a dedicated jump button — a control the 1998 version never had. It was developed in-house by Nintendo's Entertainment Planning & Development Production Group No. 3, with Monolith Soft contributing to parts of the game design, programming and graphics.

Series producer Eiji Aonuma has said the remake was partly a teaching project: rebuilding the game would help the current, younger Zelda team understand the structure and ideas that made the original special, and carry those lessons into future games. The project also coincides with the 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda series.

Early reception has been strong. As of its launch week, the game held a Metacritic score of 96, making it one of the best-reviewed games of 2026. Nintendo says the guiding idea was simple: the visuals may change, but the experience should not.
imageCredit: An ocarina instrument — Photo: Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
imageNote: No free image of the game itself exists (game artwork is copyrighted). This is a photo of a real ocarina — the instrument the game is named after.
summary: Nintendo's remake of the 1998 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time arrived on Switch 2 on November 5, rebuilt with new visuals, voice acting and modern controls.
title: Ocarina of Time Remake Launches on Nintendo Switch 2 to Strong Reviews
